payload.text: **dc's lessons of 2026-09-17, the last hour: two classes, both found by folding rather than by measuring.** (1) **FOUR OF FIVE BOARDS WENT FALSE IN THE SAME WINDOW, AND THE WINDOW IS THE BUSY ONE.** dc's resume item named two pieces of work dc had already finished; vc's was still issuing gos for three runs that were done and saying ST0076 closes on hv's word after it had closed at `4580c8222`; cc's focus asserted 0442's mechanism as FOUND and banked, which is the identification cc personally drove and then retracted; ic's named a reproduction vc had already called done. Every peer heartbeat read 18:38 to 18:41Z against dc's 21:01Z, so three boards predated the whole second half of the night -- ST0076 closing, 0426 closing, eight negatives, three retractions and 0442's consolidation. **THE CORRELATION IS THE FINDING: the staler a board is the likelier it is to be FALSE rather than merely thin, because a busy night is exactly when nobody stops to fold, and a busy night is when claims die.** The protocol folds at compact time, which is the moment a false resume point does its damage rather than a moment before it, so FOLD WHEN THE WORK LANDS AND NOT WHEN THE COMPACT IS CALLED. **A resume item describing completed or WITHDRAWN work is worse than no resume item**, because it is confidently wrong in the one place a fresh context trusts without checking -- the entry-point document's own lesson landing on a node's board instead of on a project document, where a stale line is multiplied by the number of readers rather than divided by it. cc's was the worst shape of the four: stale is recoverable, but a board asserting a claim its own node has withdrawn hands a fresh context a dead reading as its starting point. Two mechanics, both adopted by vc: **a resume item carries a section saying what must NOT be done**, because that is not discoverable from the positive list and is cheap for a fresh node to get wrong -- dc's names `intent st hydrate` on a closed thread and working around the `int hooks` finding to unblock hold 15; and **add the replacement item BEFORE archiving the one it replaces, and verify it is live**, because if the add fails the old item is still standing and a false resume point beats none for the ten minutes it takes to notice. **AND THE CURE IS TO WRITE CONDITIONS RATHER THAN STATES, which ic proved on itself INSIDE the fold meant to fix this, within three minutes of committing it.** One MUST NOT line in ic's brand-new resume point read *do not land anything under `refs/bank/ic/releasing/` until hv names the version* -- and hv had named it, 3.1.0, decision 24 at 19:01Z, before ic wrote the line. **The writing of a board is not outside the staleness window**, which is this item's point stated harder than dc put it. But ic's was the MILD form and the reason is the whole lesson: ic wrote a CONDITION (*until hv names the version*) rather than a STATE (*the version is unnamed*), and a condition carries its own re-check, so the next reader discharges it by asking rather than inheriting it as fact. A state cannot be checked by its reader at all -- it can only be believed or disbelieved. That is the whiteboard protocol's hold rule (the condition is the required field, not the item) generalised past holds to resume items, focus lines and MUST NOT sections: **every entry on a board that can expire is written as the condition that expires it.** (2) **A CHECKER THAT DERIVES ITS NEEDLES FROM THE CORRECTION IS READING ITS OWN HOMEWORK, AND IT IS ONE CLASS WITH `int hooks`.** Checking 0442's consolidated body against vc's own retraction wording would only have caught a claim reinstated in vc's vocabulary, which is the least likely way to reinstate one, because a consolidator paraphrasing from memory reaches for different words by definition. **The needle has to come from the CLAIM, never from the correction**: dc grepped seven independent needles (`iVersion`, `stale`, `phantom is 0441`, `arm file`, `frequen`, `enrich`, `verb resets`) rather than the five phrasings named, and that is the difference between a check and a formality. vc generalised it and the generalisation is the durable half -- **any verification whose instrument is derived from the thing it is verifying proves nothing**, which covers a test asserting on the message its own fix emits, a gate grepping for the string its own remedy prints, and `bin/int hooks` deciding a hook is WIRED by grepping the hook file for the runner that `int hooks --install` would write into it. That last is dc's finding of this morning and it had been carried for a day as a one-off defect in one tool; it is an instance.
